headline: Majors hold above the 200-day while momentum stretches; whales moving coins onto exchanges as funding turns expensive on leverage longs.
paragraphs: Six of seven major assets sit above their 200-day simple moving average, with BTC, ETH, SOL, XRP, and BNB all anchored in uptrend territory. DOGE and ADA are the exceptions: DOGE trades below the 200-day despite a 17.67% gain over thirty days, while ADA sits well below with the only negative MACD signal in the group and a 78.3% drawdown from its twelve-month high. No golden cross has formed yet across the board; the 50/200 separation is there but not the fresh buy signal. The regime, then, is recovery and consolidation above intermediate support, not a fresh breakout structure. BTC and ETH momentum remain overbought by RSI, both above 70, while SOL has pushed RSI to 75.2, the highest on the sheet. That extreme reading often signals either exhaustion or the tail end of a strong move; here it comes with single-digit intraday price movement, a sign momentum may be resting rather than accelerating into new highs.

MACD is above signal line on five of seven assets, including all the top-tier names. The exception, ADA, shows MACD below signal and has lost 0.56% on the day, the steepest decline in the group. For the five in momentum alignment with the uptrend, the picture is internally sound, but the RSI readings say the move has traveled far in the near term without fresh price confirmation. A momentum divergence is forming: the uptrend is intact, but the velocity that carried BTC up 22% over thirty days and SOL up 40.1% is not translating into matching price movement today. That gap between direction and daily pace is worth watching; it often precedes either a consolidation or a washout of overleveraged longs.

Funding rates on BTC and ETH are positive and climbing toward annualized cost: BTC trades at 0.0048% per eight hours (5.3% annualized) while ETH sits at 0.0096% (10.5% annualized). SOL is the outlier, running negative funding at minus 0.004% per eight hours, suggesting shorts are paying longs to hold, a sign of overcrowding on the long side there. Open interest is concentrated in BTC and ETH, at 2.23 billion and 1.53 billion dollars respectively. The long-short ratio on XRP is the most extreme at 2.46 to one, followed by DOGE at 3.93 to one, both indicators of heavily biased positioning. In the last twenty-four hours, liquidations have skewed hard toward long side: BTC saw 17.8 million dollars in long liquidations versus 2 million in shorts, and ETH showed 16.9 million longs wiped versus 3 million shorts. That asymmetry, combined with expensive funding and overbought momentum, traces a market where longs are both crowded and paying to hold the bet.

Whale flows over the last twenty-four hours show 179 million dollars net moving onto exchanges, all in BTC. The biggest single moves were into Kraken (158.7 million, then 157.8 million) and Coinbase institutional (93.2 million). Outflows occurred from the same venues, creating a churn pattern rather than a clean directional move. Over the weekly window, the picture sharpens: four consecutive weeks of net inflows onto exchanges, with the most recent week ending August 29 recording 596 million dollars onto the books. The week prior (August 22) saw 1.125 billion dollars flow onto exchanges. This three-week surge onto exchanges coincides with rising funding costs and stretched momentum, a classic setup where big holders are redistributing position while retail longs are paying to hold. Stablecoin float sits at 309.8 billion dollars, up only 1.11% over thirty days, suggesting dry powder is relatively flat; the crowd has already deployed most of what it intends to, and the margin for new buying pressure is narrow.

ETF flows tell a mixed story. BTC spot ETFs recorded a 201.9 million dollar outflow on August 28, but the five-session net is positive 924.5 million dollars, with only one day of aligned direction. The disconnect is material: traditional finance has added exposure over the longer window even as the latest print reversed. ETH ETF flows are more coherent, showing a 102.1 million dollar inflow on the latest date and 815.7 million dollars net over five sessions, with ten consecutive same-direction days. ETH is pulling steady TradFi bid; BTC inflows remain choppy. Sentiment stands at 68, labeled Greed, within a thirty-day range of 25 to 74. The crowd is confident, but the tape shows tension: longs are paying to hold, whales are moving coins onto exchanges, momentum is overbought without follow-through price action, and the ETF picture is inconsistent at the margin.

The conditions to monitor are clear. A break below the 200-day for BTC or ETH would signal the uptrend is no longer intact; neither is near that line today. A funding rate collapse or flip to negative on BTC and ETH would suggest long positioning is capitulating. A sustained reversal in the weekly whale flow direction, from onto-exchanges to off-exchanges, would indicate big holders are moving back into cold storage. And BTC ETF flows: if the outflow on August 28 extends into a second and third session, the TradFi bid may be cooling faster than the spot price reflects. For now, the regime persists above the 200-day, but the machinery underneath, funding and positioning and whale distribution, is configured for a move down, not a push higher.
